invariants.name: ftoc_repeated_param_quad
invariants.invariant: Fundamental theorem of calculus / integration-differentiation consistency: the derivative of the antiderivative F returned by integrate() must equal the integrand f away from poles, for rational functions whose irreducible quadratic factors carry free parameters
invariants.rationale: Integrand t^2*(p-3q+7t)^3/((p-3q+7t)^2+11)^2 is a new instance (new linear form, new constant 11, new parameter values) of the parameterized repeated-irreducible-quadratic class. Pre-fix, _get_real_roots returns a partial real-root set for the parameterized resultant (count_roots raises DomainError and the old code blindly returned what roots() found) and the D.evalf(chop=True) != 0 test misclassifies symbolic D, so log_to_real silently emits the antiderivative WITHOUT the log/atan terms of the factor (p-3q+7t)^2+11; the returned closed form is purely rational, its central finite difference does not match f at the sample points, and the test fails. Post-fix, _get_real_roots reports the undetermined roots (None), log_to_real bails out, and ratint falls back to the exact RootSum form, so dF/dt == f and the test passes.

"""FTOC invariant: dF/dt == f for a new parameterized rational input."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "source"))

from sympy import Integral, Symbol, integrate

t = Symbol("t", real=True)
p, q = Symbol("p", real=True), Symbol("q", real=True)
f = t**2 * (p - 3*q + 7*t)**3 / ((p - 3*q + 7*t)**2 + 11)**2
F = integrate(f, t)
assert not F.has(Integral), f"expected an evaluated antiderivative, got {F}"
step, tol = 1e-6, 1e-5
for values in (({"p": 2.5, "q": -1.25, "t": 0.7}, {"p": -4.0, "q": 3.0, "t": 1.9})):
    pt = {s: values[s.name] for s in f.free_symbols}
    pt_plus, pt_minus = dict(pt), dict(pt)
    pt_plus[t], pt_minus[t] = pt[t] + step, pt[t] - step
    forward = complex(F.subs(pt_plus).evalf(80))
    backward = complex(F.subs(pt_minus).evalf(80))
    finite_difference = (forward - backward) / (2 * step)
    target = complex(f.subs(pt).evalf(80))
    assert abs(finite_difference - target) < tol, (
        f"FTOC violated at {values}: dF/dt={finite_difference}, f={target}"
    )
print("PASS")

invariants.name: ftoc_param_quad_power_two
invariants.invariant: Fundamental theorem of calculus / integration-differentiation consistency: dF/dt must equal f for a second, structurally different parameterized family (numerator power 3, quadratic (u+2v+4t)^2+6 squared)
invariants.rationale: A different member of the same bug class (different powers, different linear form and constant) so the fix cannot succeed by accident on one shape. Pre-fix, log_to_real again drops the log/atan contribution of the repeated parameterized quadratic and the finite-difference check of F against f fails at the sample points. Post-fix the exact fallback restores the missing terms and dF/dt == f at both sample points, so the test passes. Verified: fails pre-fix, passes post-fix.

invariants.name: ftoc_double_quad_parameter
invariants.invariant: Boundary/degenerate-parameter limit: as the quadratic t^2+a has no provable real roots for free a, the antiderivative of 1/(t^2+a)^2 must still contain the arctan (complex-log) contribution; differentiation of F must reproduce f for every positive a
invariants.rationale: For the log part h = t + 4*_t*a^2 over q = _t^2 + 1/(16*a^3), pre-fix log_to_real returns exactly 0 (it finds no provably-real roots of the parameterized resultant and returns the empty result), so integrate returns only the rational part t/(2a(a+t^2)) and the arctan term is missing: dF/dt != f at the sample points and the test fails. Post-fix, _get_real_roots returns None for the undecidable parameterized factor, log_to_real returns None, and ratint supplies the correct log/arctan terms via the RootSum fallback, so dF/dt == f and the test passes.

invariants.name: ftoc_quadratic_numerator
invariants.invariant: Fundamental theorem of calculus / representation equivalence: a proper rational function with a parameterized irreducible denominator (t^2-2bt+c)/(t^2+a) must integrate to t plus the parameterized log(t^2+a)-type terms, and differentiation must recover the integrand
invariants.rationale: Pre-fix, integrate returns literally just t for this integrand: the entire log contribution coming from the irreducible quadratic t^2+a with free parameters a, b, c is silently dropped by log_to_real, so dF/dt = 1 while f evaluates to (t^2-2bt+c)/(t^2+a) at the samples and the test fails. Post-fix the undetermined-roots check makes log_to_real bail out to the exact fallback, the log terms are present, and dF/dt == f at both sample points, so the test passes.

invariants.name: ftoc_mixed_linear_quadratic
invariants.invariant: Fundamental theorem of calculus / partial-fraction decomposition consistency: 1/((t^2+a)(t-b)) decomposes into a real-root term and an irreducible-quadratic term; the antiderivative must contain BOTH contributions and differentiate back to f
invariants.rationale: New mixed input (one real pole at t=b and one parameterized complex-conjugate pair from t^2+a, with fresh parameter values). Pre-fix only the log term from the real root survives in integrate's output; the two log/atan terms from the irreducible factor t^2+a are dropped by log_to_real, so the finite difference of F misses part of f and the test fails. Post-fix all partial-fraction contributions are present and dF/dt == f at both sample points, so the test passes.

notes: All five tests were executed against both trees: the pre-fix tree (git HEAD source/sympy/integrals/rationaltools.py) and the post-fix tree (staged draft patch). Each test FAILS pre-fix (AssertionError: FTOC violated, exit 1) and PASSES post-fix (prints PASS, exit 0). Inputs (integrand shapes, coefficients, parameter values, sample points) are all new and nothing from fixtures/cases.json is referenced. The check scheme mirrors the public reproduction (80-digit evalf, central difference with step 1e-6, tolerance 1e-5) plus an explicit assertion that integrate returns an evaluated expression rather than an unevaluated Integral, as the public documentation promises. Two candidate families, (2t+a)/(t^2+a*t+b) and t/(t^2+a), were probed but PASS on both pre-fix and post-fix (handled correctly even by the buggy code), so they were excluded as non-discriminating rather than shipped as vacuous guards. A heavier family (3t^2+m*t+1)/((t^2+a)*(t^2+2a)) timed out above 150 s and was excluded for runtime reasons.
